If the elevator is falling at fifty miles per hour, jumping upwards at three miles per hour only reduces your speed to forty-seven. Plus, timing the exact millisecond of impact in complete free-fall is virtually impossible. Standing straight up breaks your spine and crushes your femur bones. Instead, immediately lie flat on your back in the center of the cabin floor. This distributes the impact deceleration force evenly across your ribs, skeleton, and body mass. 493e39e1181cbcdfa3f77d430e50da4eb92934dc.title: Why Cold Water Kills In 60 Seconds #shorts
493e39e1181cbcdfa3f77d430e50da4eb92934dc.full_text: Why do healthy swimmers drown in cold water in under sixty seconds? Most people assume hypothermia is the killer, but hypothermia takes thirty minutes to set in. The immediate killer is cold shock response. When freezing water strikes your skin, skin thermoreceptors trigger an involuntary gasp reflex. If your mouth is underwater when you gasp, you instantly inhale up to two liters of water into your lungs. Your blood pressure spikes instantly as peripheral veins contract, risking cardiac arrest. To survive, fight the instinct to swim: float on your back for ninety seconds until your breathing regulates. A vital reflex to master, before sudden immersion steals your breath...

Do not waste time calling emergency services or waiting for water to fill the cabin. Remember four words: Seatbelts off, Windows open, Children out, Exit immediately. Power windows typically function for sixty seconds before electrical shorts kill the motor.
